newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Port Arthur gunman merciless as he shot 35 victims.
newsitem.headline: Port Arthur gunman merciless as he shot 35 victims.

text.p: Gunman Martin Bryant took less than two minutes at the horrifying peak of the Port Arthur massacre to slaughter 20 people, all at point-blank or close range as they ate their lunch at the historic site's cafe.

In describing the carnage of modern Australia's worst mass murder, in which a total of 35 people died, the prosecutor admitted it was difficult for him to fully convey the confusion and horror that overwhelmed the cafe in those brief moments.

"It's difficult to describe in unemotive words what happened," prosecutor Damian Bugg told the Tasmanian Supreme Court on Tuesday, as Bryant, who has confessed to the murders, sat relaxed in the dock, occasionally smiling and smirking.

"He was in there for approximately one and a half minutes to, at the outside, two minutes. In that time he killed 20 people, attempted to kill four, wounded six and caused grievous bodily harm to one," Bugg told the hushed courtroom.

Bryant had planned the shooting spree, buying semi-automatic military-style rifles earlier in the year and hiding some of his firearms in two pianos inside his house on a quiet suburban street in the state capital, Hobart, the court heard.
He had also bought a tennis bag, measuring it in the shop with a tape measure and telling the shop assistant it needed to have strong handles to carry heavy ammunition.
On the eve of the massacre, Bryant dined with his mother, Carleen, and girlfriend Petra Wilmott at his mother's home. Bryant was talkative but did not hint at his plans.

That night he set his alarm for 6 a.m. -- something Wilmott said her wealthy, unemployed boyfriend never did -- and set off alone for the hour-long drive to Port Arthur in his yellow Volvo with a surfboard on top. He did not say where he was going.
He loaded his car with three military-style rifles, two sets of handcuffs, some rope, a hunting knife and cans of petrol.
Bryant stopped along the way at a newsagency where be bought a cigarette lighter, at a supermarket and at a petrol station where he sipped coffee and mentioned he was going surfing.
Bryant later arrived near Port Arthur at the Seascape Guesthouse where he shot the owners, David and Noelene Martin, around midday. It was David Martin's birthday.

Bryant then drove to Port Arthur, the site of a former penal colony and a popular tourist spot, stopping en route to speak to a couple whose car had broken down. Asked if he was going surfing, Bryant replied: "No, I'm going to the Isle of the Dead (off Port Arthur) to get rid of some wasps."

Bryant parked his car at Port Arthur and walked into the cafe at around 1.30 p.m., carrying a rifle concealed in the tennis bag and a video camera. He ate lunch and chatted on the cafe's balcony with some tourists.
He is said to have remarked there were a lot of wasps -- perhaps meaning White Anglo-Saxon Protestants -- but not many Japanese tourists visiting the site.
Bryant then walked to an inside table, placed his bag there and took out the rifle and opened fire, shooting people in the head, saying nothing and laughing, survivors said.
He then left the cafe and took aim at people in the Port Arthur carpark, hunting down his victims. There were few places to run and some people mistook the gunfire for staged theatrics.
Neville Quin had found his wife, Janette, shot dead in the carpark when he turned to face Bryant.

Quin ran into a vacant tourist bus, pursued by Bryant who aimed the rifle at Quin as he cowered behind a seat. Bryant said, "No one gets away from me" and fired, but Quin flinched and the bullet missed his head and struck him in the neck.
Quin escaped and miraculously survived. Others did not.

Bryant then got back into his car and drove back toward the historic site's entrance, stopping to kill Nanette Mikac and her two daughters, aged three and six, despite the mother's pleading "Please don't hurt my babies."
He shot the elder daughter dead as she hid behind a tree.

Bryant shot and killed more unsuspecting victims just entering the site, hijacked a BMW car after slaying its four occupants and then drove to a petrol station where he murdered a woman and took her boyfriend hostage in the car's boot.
He drove the BMW back to the Seascape Guesthouse, stopping at the driveway entrance to shoot at other cars heading to the guesthouse, seriously wounding some people.
He drove down the driveway, took his terrified hostage, Glenn Pears, from the boot, set fire to the BMW and holed up inisde the guesthouse where he later shot Pears.
Bryant was arrested the next morning after he set fire to the building and ran from the blaze to save himself.
